summary: Ra is a Knizia auction game where players bid Sun tokens to win sets of tiles representing ancient Egyptian civilization elements, across three escalating epochs. It's tense and quick, with elegant push-your-luck decisions about when to trigger an auction versus keep drawing tiles.
praised: Elegant, tense bidding mechanism with real psychological depth
Fast-playing and easy to teach despite strategic richness
Strong theme integration through tile types (monuments, floods, civilizations)
criticised: Can feel swingy with disaster tiles wiping out progress
Bidding math and scoring can be fiddly for newcomers
Some randomness in tile draws affects auction quality

interaction.detail: Every auction is a shared, direct competition where players bid against each other for the same set of tiles, and choosing to call Ra affects everyone's turn timing. Individual tile collections are private, but the auction pool and Ra track are entirely shared.

sources: scoring at the end of each of the three epochs across all tile categories
final epoch bonus for remaining sun value
scoring.how_you_win: Over three epochs, accumulate the most points from civilization sets, Nile/Flood tiles, monument majorities, Pharaoh tile counts, and gold, with sun tiles adding a bonus in the final epoch.
